name: Beginner
title: First Words, First Confidence
tagline: Introduce yourself, ask simple questions and master the everyday basics.
overview: A1 is where German starts to feel possible. You will build your first sentences from the ground up: sounds, greetings, core verbs, gender and the cases that hold the language together. Every lesson pairs a clear English explanation with real German you can use the same day.
levelGoal: By the end of A1 you can introduce yourself, ask and answer simple questions, shop, order food, and describe your family and daily routine in short, connected sentences.
canDo: Greet people formally and informally and introduce yourself.
Ask and answer simple questions about your home, family and work.
Order food, shop for everyday items and ask for prices.
Describe your daily routine and ask for directions.

modules.title: First Contact
modules.summary: The sounds, greetings and numbers you need to make a confident first impression.

lessons.title: The German Alphabet & Sounds
lessons.summary: Meet the alphabet, the umlauts and the German sounds that English speakers find most surprising.
objectives: Pronounce all 26 letters and the umlauts ä, ö and ü.
Distinguish the sounds ch, sch, ei and ie.
Spell your own name using the German alphabet.

lessons.title: Greetings & Introductions
lessons.summary: Greet people appropriately at any time of day and introduce yourself with name and origin.
objectives: Choose between informal du and formal Sie.
Introduce your name and where you come from.
Ask someone their name and where they are from.

lessons.title: Numbers, Dates & Time
lessons.summary: Count from zero to one hundred, tell the time the German way and talk about days and months.
objectives: Count to 100 and understand prices spoken aloud.
Tell the time using Uhr and halb.
Name the days of the week and months of the year.

modules.title: Core Sentences
modules.summary: Build your first real sentences with the two essential verbs, the present tense and questions.

lessons.title: Sein & Haben
lessons.summary: The two most important German verbs: who you are and what you have.
objectives: Conjugate sein and haben in the present tense.
Describe yourself and others using sein.
Say what you have using haben and the accusative.

lessons.title: The Present Tense
lessons.summary: Regular verb endings are your engine — learn them once and use them everywhere.
objectives: Conjugate regular verbs such as wohnen, lernen and arbeiten.
Handle stems ending in -t and -d.
Form simple statements with correct word order.

lessons.title: Questions & Question Words
lessons.summary: Ask for information with W-questions and turn statements into yes/no questions.
objectives: Use wer, was, wo, wann, wie and warum.
Form yes/no questions with verb-first word order.
Answer questions naturally with short responses.

modules.title: Nouns & Cases
modules.summary: Gender, articles and the accusative: the grammar that makes German sentences work.

lessons.title: Gender & Definite Articles
lessons.summary: Why is it der Tisch, die Tür and das Fenster? Learn how German nouns are organised.
objectives: Recognise masculine, feminine and neuter nouns with der, die and das.
Apply common gender clues for people and word endings.
Form the plural using the five main patterns.

lessons.title: The Accusative Case
lessons.summary: Mark the direct object of a sentence and use ein, eine and the accusative pronouns.
objectives: Change der to den in the accusative.
Distinguish ein from einen.
Use mich, dich, ihn and sie as object pronouns.

lessons.title: Negation & Possessives
lessons.summary: Say no correctly with nicht and kein, then say what belongs to whom.
objectives: Choose between nicht and kein.
Use mein, dein, sein and ihr before nouns.
Place nicht in the correct position in a sentence.

modules.title: Everyday Life
modules.summary: Family, food, shopping and routines — the vocabulary and phrases for daily life.

lessons.title: Family & Describing People
lessons.summary: Talk about your family and describe people using adjectives and the verb sein.
objectives: Name close and extended family members.
Use possessive articles to introduce family members.
Describe age, appearance and character in simple sentences.

lessons.title: Food, Shopping & Prices
lessons.summary: Order in a café, shop at the market and understand prices without panic.
objectives: Use polite request phrases with ich hätte gern.
Ask for prices and understand euro amounts.
Name common foods and drinks with their articles.

keyPhrase.de: Ich hätte gern einen Kaffee, bitte.
keyPhrase.en: I would like a coffee, please.

lessons.title: Daily Routine & Prepositions
lessons.summary: Describe your day with separable verbs and the prepositions um, am and im.
objectives: Conjugate separable verbs such as aufstehen and einkaufen.
Talk about times with um, am and im.
Link your daily activities in a short paragraph.

keyPhrase.de: Ich stehe um sieben Uhr auf.
keyPhrase.en: I get up at seven o'clock.
